questions.stem: This question is about gases in the atmosphere.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which of these gases has the lowest percentage by volume in the atmosphere? A argon B carbon dioxide C nitrogen D oxygen

questions.stem: This question is about alcohols. Ethanol can be manufactured using two different methods. hydration of ethene fermentation of glucose This is the equation for hydration. $\mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {4} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {5} \mathrm {O H}$

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the equation for fermentation. $\mathrm {C} _ {6} \mathrm {H} _ {1 2} \mathrm {O} _ {6} \rightarrow$

parts.label: b
parts.text: The table gives some information about the two methods.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Complete the table by giving the missing information.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using fermentation rather than hydration to produce ethanol. You should use information from the table to help your answer. advantage disadvantage

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why fermentation needs to occur in the absence of air.

parts.label: d

parts.label: d-ii

questions.stem: A student does a titration to find the concentration of potassium hydroxide solution. This is the student's method. add $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the potassium hydroxide solution to a conical flask add a few drops of methyl orange indicator to the conical flask fill a burette with dilute sulfuric acid and record the initial burette reading place the conical flask on a white tile add the acid from the burette to the mixture in the conical flask, swirling the flask continuously when the indicator changes colour at the end point, record the final burette reading Repeat the titration to obtain concordant results.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the name of the most suitable piece of apparatus to measure out $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of potassium hydroxide solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the colour of methyl orange in potassium hydroxide solution and in dilute sulfuric acid. colour in potassium hydroxide solution colour in dilute sulfuric acid

parts.label: c
parts.text: State why the student places the conical flask on a white tile.

parts.label: d
parts.text: State why the student swirls the flask continuously.

parts.label: e
parts.text: State what is meant by the term concordant results.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The student finds that $ 1 5. 0 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sulfuric acid of concentration $ 0. 1 8 0 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ neutralises $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of potassium hydroxide solution. This is the equation for the reaction. $2 \mathrm {K O H} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} \rightarrow \mathrm {K} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ Calculate the concentration of the potassium hydroxide solution. $\mathrm {c o n c e n t r a t i o n} =$ $\mathrm {m o l} / \mathrm {d m} ^ {3}$

parts.label: g
parts.text: This is the ionic equation for the reaction between an acid and an alkali. $\mathrm {H} ^ {+} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {O H} ^ {-} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {I})$ Explain why the $ \mathrm{O H}^{-} $ ion is a proton acceptor in this reaction.

parts.label: b

parts.label: d
parts.text: Oxygen forms at the positive electrode.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Complete the half-equation for the formation of oxygen at the positive electrode.

parts.label: d-iii
parts.text: State why the formation of oxygen at the positive electrode is an oxidation reaction.
